column2: Bombay Hospital & Medical Research Centre v. Asha Jaiswal and Ors.
column3: 2021 INSC 801; 2021 SCC OnLine SC 1149; CA 1658 of 2010
column12: Whether a hospital and doctor were negligent in treating a patient who died, where NCDRC relied on res ipsa loquitur and the lack of an operation theatre.
column13: NCDRC order set aside and complaint dismissed; no expert evidence of negligence; Rs 5 lakh already paid treated as ex gratia.
column14: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab

column2: M/s Sheth M.L. Vaduwala Eye Hospital v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. and Ors.
column12: Whether a hospital can be indemnified by the insurer under professional indemnity policies taken by its doctors after negligent cataract surgeries at an eye camp.
column13: Hospital cannot claim indemnity under policies obtained by the doctors for their own professional liability; the negligence finding was against the hospital itself.

column2: Dr. (Mrs.) Chanda Rani Akhouri v. Dr. M.A. Methusethupathi
column12: Whether the treating doctors were negligent in post-operative care after a kidney transplant that ended in the patient's death.
column13: No negligence; doctors are not liable merely because the patient could not be saved, and an error of judgment or accident is not proof of negligence.
column14: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab

column2: Harnek Singh and Ors. v. Gurmit Singh and Ors.
column12: Whether a surgeon and hospital were negligent in failing to detect bowel perforation after surgery, and what weight Medical Council of India findings carry.
column13: NCDRC erred in ignoring the evidence; MCI findings on the doctor's conduct are highly relevant; negligence established and Rs 25 lakh with 6% interest awarded.

column2: Devarakonda Surya Sesha Mani v. Care Hospital, Institute of Medical Sciences
column12: Whether the death of a patient at a Visakhapatnam hospital resulted from medical negligence and delayed treatment.
column13: NCDRC dismissal upheld; not every death in a hospital is medical negligence and the Court will not second-guess the doctors' treatment decisions.
column14: Supreme Court decisions on the medical negligence test (not named in the order)

column2: Nagarmal Modi Sewa Sadan v. Prem Prakash Rajagaria and Ors.
column12: Who must pay compensation for negligence by doctors working in a hospital: the hospital or the doctors' insurer.
column13: NCDRC finding of negligence left undisturbed; the insurer must reimburse to the extent of its policy liability and the hospital pays the rest jointly and severally.
column14: Sheth M.L. Vaduwala Eye Hospital v. Oriental Insurance Co. (distinguished)

column2: Upendra Kaul v. S.C. Mathur and Ors.
column12: Whether NCDRC's adverse observations against a cardiologist and AIIMS after a patient's death following angioplasty were justified.
column13: Adverse observations against the doctor and hospital set aside; the complainants produced no independent expert evidence of negligence.

column2: CPL Ashish Kumar Chauhan (Retd.) v. Commanding Officer and Ors.
column11: CPA 1986 / HIV and AIDS Act 2017 / medical negligence
column12: Whether an air force veteran who contracted HIV from a blood transfusion at a military hospital was owed compensation for medical negligence.
column13: NCDRC order reversed; the Air Force and Army are vicariously liable and must pay about Rs 1.54 crore, with directions under the HIV Act.
column14: Savita Garg v. Director, National Heart Institute; Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences v. Prasanth S. Dhananka

column2: Mrs. Kalyani Rajan v. Indraprastha Apollo Hospital and Ors.
column3: 2023 INSC 921; 2023 SCC OnLine SC 1355; CA 10347 of 2010
column12: Whether a patient's cardiac arrest after neurosurgery showed negligent post-operative care, and whether res ipsa loquitur applies.
column13: No negligence; res ipsa loquitur needs a clear 'res' and strong evidence, so the NCDRC dismissal was upheld.
column14: Martin F. D'Souza v. Mohd. Ishfaq

column2: M.A. Biviji v. Sunita and Ors.
column12: Whether a forceful nasotracheal intubation and the later complications amounted to medical negligence by the doctors and hospital.
column13: Negligence not proved; NCDRC compensation set aside; duty of care, breach and resulting damage must all be shown.
column14: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab

column2: Jyoti Devi v. Suket Hospital and Ors.
column12: Whether compensation was adequate for post-operative negligence after appendicitis surgery left a needle in the patient's abdomen.
column13: District Forum award of Rs 5 lakh with 9% interest and Rs 50,000 costs restored; the lower reductions and the eggshell-skull reasoning were set aside.
column14: Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences v. Prasanth S. Dhananka; Balram Prasad v. Kunal Saha

column2: P.N. Gupta v. Rajinder Singh Dogra
column11: CPA 1986 / medical negligence and informed consent
column12: Whether a surgeon's operative and post-operative care, and the consent taken for further surgeries, met the required standard of care in a patient's death.
column13: Negligence upheld on several counts (surgical care, delayed referral to a liver specialist, poor records, no consent); NCDRC's Rs 7 lakh compensation stands.
column14: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab; Samira Kohli v. Dr. Prabha Manchanda

column2: D.C. Malviya (Since Deceased) through LRs v. Dr. A.H. Memon (Since Deceased) through LRs and Ors.
column12: Whether the NCDRC's compensation for a patient's death after an endoscopic polypectomy should be enhanced.
column13: SLPs dismissed; NCDRC's lump-sum award (Rs 3 lakh, plus Rs 50,000 each from two other parties) held reasonable and left undisturbed.

column2: Neeraj Sud and Anr. v. Jaswinder Singh (Minor) and Anr.
column12: Whether worsening of a minor's eye condition after ptosis surgery at PGI Chandigarh showed negligence by the surgeon.
column13: NCDRC order set aside and State Commission dismissal restored; a poor surgical outcome alone is not negligence without proof of lack of skill or care.

column2: Bherulal Bhimaji Oswal (Dead) through LRs v. Madhusudan N. Kumbhare
column12: Whether an eye surgeon was negligent in post-operative care after cataract surgery that ended in loss of vision.
column13: Negligence established without expert evidence; NCDRC order set aside and the Rs 3.5 lakh compensation restored.

column2: Dr. Mohan v. State of Tamil Nadu
column11: s 304 Part I and s 304A IPC
column12: Whether a doctor who told a nurse by phone to give an injection can be charged with culpable homicide.
column13: Culpable homicide charge under s 304 Part I quashed; trial to proceed only under s 304A (death by negligence).
column14: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab

column2: Managing Director, Kamineni Hospitals v. Peddi Narayana Swami and Anr.
column12: Whether a hospital is vicariously liable for a doctor's negligence causing a patient's death, and whether the Rs 15 lakh compensation was right.
column13: Negligence finding upheld; the hospital's compensation reduced to Rs 10 lakh with accrued interest.

column2: Deep Nursing Home and Anr. v. Manmeet Singh Mattewal and Ors.
column12: Whether NCDRC could find negligence in antenatal care when the complaint pleaded only post-delivery negligence.
column13: NCDRC order and State Commission judgment set aside and the complaint dismissed; the complainant must refund Rs 10 lakh to the doctor.

column2: Kumud Lall v. Suresh Chandra Roy (Dead) through LRs and Ors.
column11: CPA 1986 s 13(7); Order XXII CPC; s 306 Succession Act 1925
column12: Whether a medical negligence complaint survives against the legal heirs of a doctor who died during the case.
column13: Heirs may be substituted but are liable only to the extent of the estate; the consumer forum must first decide whether negligence is proved.

column2: Supriya Kumari M.C. v. State of Kerala and Ors.
column12: Whether an off-duty anaesthetist can be prosecuted for a patient's death after a nurse gave a painkiller on her phone advice.
column13: Prosecution quashed; no gross negligence shown and the expert panel had no anaesthetist.
column14: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab
